Q1: Which list of protected "automation paths" should the plan-phase auto-approve gate check the plan's "Files likely to change" section against? (This checkout has no automation-path grant guard, so it may exist only on `stable`.)
Choices:
A) Reuse the implement-side grant guard's own path classifier and grant parser on the `stable` target branch, so the plan gate and the implement guard cannot drift. If that guard is missing on the branch, the plan stops with `BLOCKED` and does not invent a list. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Define a new fixed list of prefixes in the plan gate (`.github/`, `.claude/`, `workflow-templates/`, `scripts/`, `prompts/`) and pin it equal to the guard with a contract test.
C) Reuse the existing `FILES_SECTION_FILE` scripts/ rejection list already in `plan.yml` (lines ~1650-1700).
Q2: When the gate holds back auto-approval, how should the poller's stall-recovery `auto_approve` (fires after `STALL_THRESHOLD_AWAITING_APPROVAL_MINUTES`, default 60) treat that issue?
Choices:
A) Make the stall-recovery `auto_approve` action respect the hold too: `plan.yml` posts a trusted, pipeline-authored marker comment listing the ungranted paths, and the poller skips `auto_approve` while that marker is the newest plan outcome, so only a human `/approved` (after adding grants) moves it forward. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Change only `plan.yml`, as the issue's affected-files list says. Stall recovery may still auto-approve after 60 minutes, and the implement guard will reject again safely, but with the same fingerprint.
C) Change only `plan.yml`, and have it also add `ai:scope-blocked`, which already keeps stall recovery from acting.
